children: Weak credit transmission, prolonged property correction and subdued private demand are likely to prevent a meaningful recovery and constrain growth into 2027 for China, Julius Baer economist Sophie Altermatt writes in a note. China's economy remained highly uneven in August as stronger industrial production and robust exports contrasted with further weakness in consumption, investment and property activity, she adds. Weakening credit dynamics confirm a weak appetite for loans among households and businesses, she says. There will likely be faster fiscal execution to help stabilize growth toward year end, but not to generate a broad-based recovery, Julius Baer says. The bank maintains its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 4.5%, the low end of the official target range.(jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
